entities.span: Noting that `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` does **not** answer the reference project's anchor bug: that shape (a value read as an object when it was an array) came from a wrong declared type, which no strictness flag disagrees with; it is answered by generated types plus Zod parsing at the boundary.
TypeScript, `strict` plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `verbatimModuleSyntax`
rejected_spans: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` catches unchecked array and record access.

entities.span: Single application, no services
rejected_spans: One developer, expected users in the tens. A monolith is the only pattern that is cheap to build, debug and operate at this size.

entities.span: Node, current Active LTS line, pinned in `.nvmrc` and `engines`. Confirm the exact LTS line at scaffold time.
rejected_spans: One version across local, CI and Vercel, so a version difference is never a suspect during debugging.

rejected_spans: Refuses to resolve a package that was never declared, so the dependency list stays honest.

entities.span: Next.js 16.3, App Router
rejected_spans: Current stable and LTS as of 3 August 2026. Turbopack is the default builder in 16.

entities.span: Server Components for reads, Server Actions for writes. Every Supabase call and every session check runs on the server. No database credential and no query shape reaches the browser.
Postgres, hosted by Supabase
rejected_spans: Relational data with real relationships, and `pgvector` available if the deferred retrieval tool ever arrives.

entities.span: `@supabase/supabase-js` with `@supabase/ssr`, no object relational mapper
rejected_spans: Every query carries the caller's token, so row level security applies by construction. There is no code path that can quietly bypass it.

entities.span: Postgres functions, hand written SQL. Anything that must be atomic (the feature 10 usage gate above all) is one statement in the database, not a read then write in application code.
Supabase CLI, hand written SQL files in git, local stack in Docker. Tests run against a real Postgres with the real policies applied.
rejected_spans: The repository is the source of truth for schema and policy.

entities.span: Supabase Auth, OAuth only, Google and GitHub. No transactional email service and no verification flow needed in v1.
rejected_spans: Two providers cover the named audience.

entities.span: Row level security in Postgres, plus a session check in the protected layout and again in every Server Action. The database is the guarantee. The layout check makes the denial visible.
rejected_spans: The per action check exists because a Server Action is a callable endpoint whatever page renders it.

entities.span: Publishable key (`sb_publishable_…`) in the browser. Secret key (`sb_secret_…`) only inside `src/lib/supabase/secret.ts`, see binding rule 1. The legacy `anon` and `service_role` JWT keys are deprecated by the end of 2026 and are not used at all.
rejected_spans: The current Supabase key format.

entities.span: Zod 4 at every boundary
rejected_spans: Nothing untrusted enters the application unparsed: the Adzuna response, every model output, every form input, every environment variable.

entities.span: react-hook-form with the Zod resolver
rejected_spans: The profile form is long, and per field errors without a server round trip matter there.

entities.span: None. URL search params plus `useTransition`
rejected_spans: Filter state in the URL is what feature 18 needs anyway, and `useTransition` keeps previous results on screen during a refetch, which is the direct fix for the repeat search wipes results bug.

entities.span: A `Result` discriminated union at every boundary
rejected_spans: Under `strict`, the data cannot be read without first narrowing the union, so ignoring a failure is a compile error rather than a habit.

entities.span: AI SDK 7 with direct provider packages, one key per vendor
rejected_spans: Keeps personal data flowing only to the vendors the privacy notice names, and keeps the AI layer independent of the hosting choice.

entities.span: A checked in module, keys in environment variables
rejected_spans: A model change is a reviewable commit that can trigger the eval harness. What is deployed always matches what is in git.

entities.span: Adzuna REST API
rejected_spans: Already decided, terms already checked, and it supports the structured filters feature 18 needs.

rejected_spans: First party Next.js support with no adapter to keep working, preview deployment per push, free tier for a non commercial project.
